description: `DocAccess` and the boundaries above it catch `Forbidden`, `Unauthorized` and `RpcClientError`. `GetDoc` can also fail with `DocNotFound`, so `useDocAccess` doesn't take the query, and the error names what's left. `useDocAccessResult` takes it, and returns a `Result<Doc, DocNotFound>`: reading `.title` off it doesn't type-check either.

errors.message:
Argument of type 'Query<{ readonly body: string; readonly id: number; readonly title: string; readonly updatedBy: string; }, DocNotFound | Forbidden | RpcClientError | Unauthorized, DocsClient>' is not assignable to parameter of type 'Query<{ readonly body: string; readonly id: number; readonly title: string; readonly updatedBy: string; }, DocNotFound | Forbidden | RpcClientError | Unauthorized, DocsClient> & { ...; }'.
  Property 'UnhandledErrors' is missing in type 'Query<{ readonly body: string; readonly id: number; readonly title: string; readonly updatedBy: string; }, DocNotFound | Forbidden | RpcClientError | Unauthorized, DocsClient>' but required in type '{ readonly UnhandledErrors: "DocNotFound"; }'.

Property 'title' does not exist on type 'Result<{ readonly body: string; readonly id: number; readonly title: string; readonly updatedBy: string; }, DocNotFound>'.
  Property 'title' does not exist on type 'Failure<{ readonly body: string; readonly id: number; readonly title: string; readonly updatedBy: string; }, DocNotFound>'.

title: The data hook compiles only when nothing is left

description: Read through `Session`, a doc can still fail with `Forbidden` or `DocNotFound`: both come back in the `Result`. Forgetting one is a type error that names it.

errors.message:
Argument of type '{ DocNotFound: () => React.JSX.Element; }' is not assignable to parameter of type 'ValueTagHandlers<DocNotFound | Forbidden> & {}'.
  Property 'Forbidden' is missing in type '{ DocNotFound: () => React.JSX.Element; }' but required in type 'ValueTagHandlers<DocNotFound | Forbidden>'.

title: What's left must be matched exhaustively

description: Under `DocAccess`, the failure is `DocNotFound` and nothing else. An `Unauthorized` can't reach this component (`Session` caught it), so a case for it is a type error, not dead code.

errors.message: Type '() => React.JSX.Element' is not assignable to type 'never'.

title: You can't handle an error a boundary already caught

description: `Session` already catches `Unauthorized`. Each tag has one place in a chain, so a boundary inside it that lists `Unauthorized` again is a type error that names the tag.

errors.message:
Type '["Unauthorized"]' is not assignable to type 'readonly ["Unauthorized"] & { readonly AlreadyHandledAbove: "Unauthorized"; }'.
  Property 'AlreadyHandledAbove' is missing in type '["Unauthorized"]' but required in type '{ readonly AlreadyHandledAbove: "Unauthorized"; }'.

title: A boundary can't catch what one above it catches

description: The root declares, as a type, what its queries can fail with: everything the docs RPC client can. A tag none of those errors has is a type error, and the compiler suggests the one you meant.

errors.message: Type '"Forbiden"' is not assignable to type '"DocNotFound" | "EmptyTitle" | "Forbidden" | "RpcClientError" | "Unauthorized"'. Did you mean '"Forbidden"'?

title: A boundary catches tags of the root's errors

description: The root's client is built from the RPC client's layer. A query that needs another service (`Analytics` here) doesn't type-check at any boundary under it.

errors.message:
Argument of type 'Query<number, never, Analytics>' is not assignable to parameter of type 'Query<number, never, DocsClient | QueryCache>'.
  Type 'Analytics' is not assignable to type 'DocsClient | QueryCache'.
    Type 'Analytics' is not assignable to type 'DocsClient'.
      Types of property 'Service' are incompatible.
        Type '{ readonly views: Effect<number, never, never>; }' is missing the following properties from type '{ readonly GetDoc: <const AsQueue extends boolean = false, const Discard = false>(input: { readonly id: number; }, options?: { readonly headers?: Input | undefined; readonly context?: Context<never> | undefined; readonly discard?: Discard | undefined; } | undefined) => Effect<...>; readonly ListDocs: <const AsQueue ...': GetDoc, ListDocs, RenameDoc

title: A query can only use services the client provides

description: A boundary that catches `DocNotFound` too leaves nothing, so its data hook takes the query and returns the doc itself: no `Result`, nothing to match. `useSession(docList)` is the same: `Session` and the boundaries above it catch everything `ListDocs` can fail with. This file compiles.
title: Once every error is caught, the data hook returns the data
